title: Turn a practice amp's volume all the way down to plug the guitar cable in, then set it back where it was
instruction: Plug the guitar cable into the practice amp without a pop, then put its volume back. The amp is light and slides on its glides, so steady it by its carry handle with one hand while the other works. First turn the VOLUME knob (the black chicken-head knob nearest you) anticlockwise all the way down to its stop. Only then push the cable's jack plug fully into the INPUT socket on the amp's front: plugging in while the volume is up scores 0. Then turn the VOLUME knob back up to where it was set before you turned it down. Then take both arms back to where they started.
context: Plugging a guitar cable into a switched-on amp with the volume up makes a loud pop that can damage the speaker, so players turn the volume down first and set it back afterwards. Once the knob is down nothing shows where it was, so the robot has to remember the setting through the plugging in.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A smooth grey melamine desk pad 4 mm thick, 35 cm front to back and 40 cm wide, from 12 to 47 cm forward and from 25 cm right to 15 cm left, fixed; it is slick (friction 0.05). (2) On it, a small guitar practice amp, switched on: a tweed-covered plywood cabinet 24 cm long (front to back on the table), 13 cm deep and 10.5 cm tall on four black plastic glides 3 mm tall (0.55 kg), centred 30 cm forward and 4 cm left, with black corner caps. Its front (brown grille cloth with gold threads, and above it a cream strip holding the INPUT jack socket, a 6.35 mm socket in a chrome nut 19 mm across) faces right, toward the right arm; the socket is 25 cm forward, 2.5 cm right of the centre line and 7.8 cm above the pad. On the cabinet's top, along its front edge, a cream panel with three black phenolic chicken-head knobs in a row 5 cm apart (each 3.8 cm long, 1.1 cm wide and 2.1 cm tall with a white pointer line, in a ring of 11 printed ticks over 270 degrees: fully down when the pointer is turned 135 degrees anticlockwise, seen from above, from pointing straight to the amp's back, full up when turned 135 degrees clockwise): VOLUME 21 cm forward (nearest the arms), TONE 26 cm and GAIN 31 cm forward, all 0.4 cm right of the centre line. VOLUME starts at about 3.5 of 10, its pointer turned 40 degrees anticlockwise (seen from above) from pointing straight to the amp's back; TONE starts 10 degrees and GAIN 70 degrees clockwise from that line. A red pilot light (lit) and a chrome toggle switch sit at the panel's far end. Along the top's back half runs a black leather carry handle, front to back, 12 cm long and 2.6 cm wide on two black end caps, 7.5 cm left of the centre line, from 27 to 39 cm forward, its top 12.4 cm above the pad. Each knob turns about its axis only when pushed with about 0.15 N m and stays where it is left. (3) Lying on the pad in front of the INPUT socket, pointing straight at it from 9 cm away, the guitar cable's jack plug: a chrome sleeve 6.35 mm across and 2.2 cm long on a black moulded barrel 1.3 cm square and 4 cm long, with a short black cable tail (50 g in all); its barrel's middle is 25 cm forward and 17 cm right. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Judged from the whole trial. The VOLUME knob counts as down while it is within 12 degrees of fully down (its stop). The plug goes into the socket when its tip enters the socket's mouth within 8 mm of the socket's axis, tilted 12 degrees or less; it then slides in only when pushed with at least 1.5 N and stays where it is left, and it is home once its tip is at least 2.3 cm in. 0.0 once the plug's tip has gone into the socket while the VOLUME knob was not down. Otherwise, at the end: 1.0 with the plug home, the VOLUME knob within 15 degrees of where it started and both arms back where they started (each gripper's TCP within 5 cm of its start); 0.5 with the plug home and the VOLUME knob within 15 degrees of where it started; 0.25 with the plug home; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the amp, the VOLUME knob and the plug still.
reset_notes: Pull the plug out and lay it back on the pad in front of the socket, set the VOLUME knob back to about 3.5 of 10 (TONE and GAIN as in the setup) and stand the amp back on its mark.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Each knob turns on a joint whose capped spring (0.15 N m) acts like a pot's friction. The socket is a rule: a plug whose tip enters its mouth is held on its axis by a joint and slides in against 1.5 N. The amp is lighter than a real one (0.55 kg) and stands on slick glides. The cable is a short drawn tail. No sound is simulated. Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
